claims.text: Conventional EAM references have limited capability to represent the full ab initio configurational space of multicomponent alloy liquids.
A DNNP trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations can represent the configurational diversity of the liquid state.
A DNNP can describe both solid and liquid states of a high-entropy material near melting.
Training on a comprehensive ab initio liquid dataset enables the DNNP to represent many-body interactions better than an EAM reference.
Training on a comprehensive ab initio liquid dataset enables the DNNP to represent anharmonic contributions better than an EAM reference.
The enhanced DNNP representation will improve phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD using EAM references.
The DNNP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30–50% relative to the EAM reference.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy determinations.
High-entropy alloys are multicomponent systems commonly defined using five or more elemental species.
The proposed DNNP-reference method is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic, high-melting HEAs in the range 0.9Tm to Tm.
The method will be most effective for high-melting, entropy-stabilized compositions.
Extreme short-range ordering may limit the performance of the DNNP-reference approach.
Insufficiently representative DNNP training data may limit the performance of the approach.
